Heard on I.A. No.22894/2025 , third application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of BNSS, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.
Appellant's earlier applications were dismissed.

2 . This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 19.03.2011 passed by Special Judge,
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Sagar (M.P.) in Special Case No.31/2010, whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Conviction U/s.

entities.text:
Special Judge,
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Sagar (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Imprisonment Fine
In lieu of default 450 of IPC R.I. for 7 years Rs.1000/- Additional R.I. for 6 months 376(2)(g) of IPC Life imprisonment Rs.1000/- Additional R.I. for 6 months 3.
Counsel appearing on behalf of appellant submitted that the appellant is in jail since 15/11/2009.
Appellant was convicted for commission of offence punishable under Sections 450 and 376(2)(g) of IPC.

It is also submitted that application for suspension of custodial sentence and grant of bail of co-accused in the case namely one Ramesh was allowed by this Court, vide order dated 29/08/2025 in Cr.A. No. 867/2011.
Case of the appellant is similar to him.
The appellant is in jail for last 16 years.
Co- 2 CRA-1018-2011 accused was granted bail on the basis of judgment Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Saudan Singh Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh [SLP (Cri.) No. 4633/2021].

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State prays for some time to file objection.
On being asked, learned Government Advocate submitted that it cannot be denied that the appellant is in jail since 15/11/2009.
It is also submitted by him that co-accused Ramesh was granted bail on the ground that he was in jail for last more than 10 years.

5. Since Government Advocate is unable to deny factual aspect of parity and period of custody,
therefore, grating time to file reply on said facts will be futile exercise.
6.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7 . Considering the parity of appellant with co-accused- Ramesh and the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Saudan Singh (supra) as well as the period of incarceration of 16 years undergone by the appellant,
we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.
8. Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I.A. No.22894/2025 is allowed.

9 . It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of 3 CRA-1018-2011 the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 11.12.2025 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
10. List the matter for final hearing in due course.
 (VISHAL DHAGAT) (ANURADH  JUDGE JU  skt Arvind vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178738224/
